name: Laghuu
catalog_citation: Edmondson, Jerold A. & Lama Ziwo. 1999. Laghuu or Xá Phó, a new language of the Yi group. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 22.1: 1-10.
catalog_locator: p. 5 sec. 2.5 'Tones' (page image viewed); p. 3 sec. 2.0; p. 8-9 (scanned of same scan)
catalog_quote: [p.3] One obvious feature of Laghuu is the word structure. While individual Laghuu morphemes are monosyllabic, words are typically disyllabic compounds, as in the other Yi languages. The syllable may be analyzed into an initial, a rhyme, and a tone. ... [p.5] 2.5. Tones. There are five tones in Laghuu. See Figure 2. This language does not appear to have noticeable tense/lax voice quality contrast. ... [p.8-9] There are five distinctive tones in this language (see Figure 2). There is also a tone sandhi phenomenon where 21 becomes 24, before another syllable with a 33 tone ... A 55 tone often develops a falling component at the end of a word, becoming 54 or 53.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: all three quoted passages (p.3 sec. 2.0, p.5 sec. 2.5, pp.8-9) are verbatim in the held sealang scan of Edmondson & Lama 1999 (page image p.5 viewed; scanned for pp.3, 8-9). (2) Deciding source is a 1999 primary phonology article by the fieldworkers with instrumental tone plots; Glottolog 5.1 has no grammar or fuller phonology for Laghuu (3 refs total: this article, Fried 2000 MA on Phu Kha, Abadie 1924 wordlist).312-314) gives the same five-tone system (24, 54, 44, 33, 21; the 1999 '55' is written 54, consistent with the 1999 note that 55 falls word-finally), confirms it at a second location (Son La)

sources.quote: p.313: 'Xa Pho has only one rising tone with the value 24. The other tones have the shapes 54, 44, 33, and 21.' p.313 sec. 4.2: a second location (Son La) 'The tonal system appears to be identical to Lao Cai'. Initials, rhymes, nasal codas, velar+lateral clusters described; no mention of stress, accent, or syllable prominence anywhere in the chapter's Xa Pho section (grep of full text for stress/accent/iamb/sesquisyllabic: only hits are in the Phu Kha section? none for Xa Pho).
